answer: Carrier-verified subscription binding: an agent gains influence only after binding one mobile subscription its carrier confirms as active, KYC-checked, and tied to a distinct device. The carrier publishes a signed proof, one line per identity, and duplicate or recycled lines are rejected. Abuse revokes the proof, so a line cannot be recycled for the next puppet. A farm thus needs one real, paid subscription per fake, with its own fee, device, and check — a pearl cannot back two identities, a raven needs a separate roost per master, and at the wharf each line is inspected before docking.
